newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly higher Thursday in line with LME copper prices overnight after an 850 tonne fall in LME warehouse copper stocks to 153,825 tonnes.
COMEX copper stocks rose 141 short tons to 45,608 short tons Wednesday.
COMEX May copper was called unchanged to up 0.2 cent from Wednesday's close of 105.15 cents a lb after trading from 105.30 to 105.50 cents on ACCESS.
Support is seen around 105.00 cents still, with resistance around 107.50 in the near term.

But daily momentum oscillators remain weak for COMEX May copper, and the contract's five day moving average remains below its 21-day average and its 55-day average, after the contract retreated from eight-month highs seen in March.
The COMEX May/July spread eased back further Wednesday to around 1.10 cents from 1.70 cents Tuesday, and from around 3.5 cents in March, as tightness in the prompt market has eased.

Steady economic growth in the U.S. and reviving demand in Europe and Asia are seen supporting copper prices, but China's purchases are seen likely to be limited until later in the year, while supply/demand surplus is still seen likely globally later in the year.
